text:
Maya: quick question — when the ingest service fires the `IngestErrorRateHigh` alert, which PagerDuty policy actually gets paged? I looked in the runbooks but couldn't find the mapping.

Sam: it should be `pagerduty:ingest-escalation` in labels. That policy forwards to the `eng_oncall_general` schedule first, then escalates to `ingest_oncall` after 10m. docs: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/ingest-alerts-mapping

Jin: is `eng_oncall_general` the SRE rotation or the platform rotation? want to make sure the right people are waking up for infra vs app issues.

Sam: `eng_oncall_general` is the SRE rotation (pagerduty schedule id: PD-SRE-GEN). `ingest_oncall` is the owning team schedule for the ingest microservice (PD-INGEST). if reloads/rollouts are expected during deploys we silence via a deploy tag — otherwise pages land on SRE.

OpsBot: NOTE: recent deploys annotated with `deploy_id` will suppress `severity: warning` alerts for 15m if silenced by `deploy-silence` tag. See #deploys for how to add this.

Leah: can we also tweak the rule? current noise from bursty 1m spikes is causing duplicate pages. suggest increasing for: 1m -> 5m and set threshold from 3% -> 5% (we saw a lot of harmless transient errors during the Canary).

Sam: agree on increasing `for` to 5m. here's what I propose we change in alerting-rules/prometheus/ingest.yaml (copy of current rule):

```
alert: IngestErrorRateHigh
expr: job:ingest_errors:rate1m{job="ingest"} > 0.03
for: 1m
labels:
  severity: page
  team: ingest
  pagerduty: ingest-escalation
annotations:
  runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/ingest-runbook
```

Sam: proposed change:

```
expr: job:ingest_errors:rate5m{job="ingest"} > 0.05
for: 5m
```

Jin: that sounds reasonable. question: if we change the `pagerduty` label, does that require a PD config change? i.e., will it create a new escalation route?

Sam: as long as label value matches an existing PD integration on the alertmanager -> pagerduty routing map, no PD-side change is needed. it's controlled by alertmanager routing rules in `ops/alertmanager/config.yaml`. snippet: 

```
- match_re:
    pagerduty: "ingest.*"
  receiver: pagerduty-ingest
  continue: false
```

Henry: I can open the PR to bump the rule and update the docs page with the exact mapping. who should review?

Leah: add `@Sam` and `@Jin` as reviewers, they know the PD bits. also please add a short note in the PR about the deploy silence behaviour so QA understands the change window.

Maya: also one last ask — can we add a link to the ingest Grafana dashboard in the runbook so oncall can triage faster? current runbook only lists logs.

Sam: good call. runbook link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/ingest-service-overview. I'll edit the runbook in the same PR.

Henry: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-config/pull/482 — includes updated rule + runbook link + note about `deploy_silence` policy. tagging reviewers now.

Maya: thanks all — please ping here when the PR is merged and when PD routing is live so I can update the oncall checklist. :thumbsup:

OpsBot: Deploy note: config PR will trigger `ops-ci/validate` and `ops-ci/alertmanager-lint`. expect CI ~10m after PR.

Sam: once CI passes I'll merge and post a follow-up here. if anyone wants to test, you can create a test alert with `label: pagerduty=ingest-escalation` in `promtool` staging.

Maya: great, marking this resolved for now. thanks!
